title: How can ice help answer our climate questions?
author: Emma
body:
This Earth Day, the APT Foundation shines a light on the incredible contribution made by Antarctic Science Foundation in researching our climate.

Later this year, an Antarctic expedition will venture South to drill an ice core dating back more than a million years. This project will require an inland trek of over 1,300 kilometres from the coast to establish a remote drill site and camp to house equipment and researchers over the summer months.

The goal is ambitious in scale but will make a vital contribution to the climate puzzle. Within this rare ice are tiny bubbles that act as pockets containing air and chemicals captured throughout time. Analysis of these gases and chemicals will provide a snapshot of the Earth’s climate and atmospheric composition. Researchers can use this information to make more accurate predictions of climate stability and help us understand the strategies required to mitigate the effects of climate disruption.

Other climate initiatives Antarctic Science Foundation contribute to:

• Climate prediction for all Australians.

• Fire, flood and drought prediction and mitigation.

• Managing economic and sustainable fisheries.

• Carbon capture and abatement via nature’s systems.

• Increasing the health of our oceans.

• Improving global biodiversity.

• Protection of Antarctic wildlife.

The APT Foundation supports Antarctic Science Foundation in their research. We believe in the value and potential of Antarctica to provide the answers we need to sustain our way of life on this planet. If you’d like to donate to Antarctic Science Foundation please follow the link here.
